[b]Completed with 100% of achievements, earned after 39 hours of play. (more on that below)[/b]

[h1]Overall[/h1]

Ultimate Chicken Horse is one of the few games that's actually more fun than it looks.  I will even go as far to say that it is one of the best party games of all time.  I haven't played a party game that has maintained my interest longer, or has been a bigger hit with guests of all ages.  It's easy to learn, only a little bit harder to master, but interestingly, experienced players won't necessarily stomp the novices every time.  A large selection of options, modifiers, and levels extended my interest, even after dozens of hours of play. 

[table]
[tr]
	[th]Pros[/th]
	[th]Cons[/th]
[/tr]
[tr]
	[td]
✅You can mix both local, and online multiplayer
✅Great execution of a fun concept
✅Good selection of both official, and community levels
✅ Items that interact with each other provide extra versatility and extend replay value
✅Lots of modifiers even the playing field against experienced players.
[/td]
	[td]
❌Multiplayer only (mostly)
❌Capped at a max of four players
[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Ultimate Chicken Horse is based around collectively building a 2D platformer level with your friends.  Each round has two parts.  First, each player gets roughly 20 seconds to set a platform, obstacle, or trap, then you must all play the level you created.  If it's too easy, and you all complete it, no points.  If it's too hard, and no one completes it, no points. You have to find that sweet spot between building a level that kills your friends, while still being able to survive it yourself.  You then repeat this loop, and either add or remove stuff from the same level, until one player has scored enough points to win. It's really a simple concept, but it's executed brilliantly.  

[h1]Multiplayer and Single Player[/h1]

You can technically play Ultimate Chicken Horse single-player.  There are plenty of solo "challenge" levels built by the community. However, if that's your main intention, don't get it.  It's designed for multiplayer, and shines like a jewel in that mode.

One of the features I appreciate most is that you can mix local multiplayer with online multiplayer.  This allows me, and my daughter to play on my PC with two of my friends online, all together.  So many multiplayer games don't do this, and I'm not sure why.  Other games may support both local and online multiplayer capabilities, but it's not at the same time.  You have to do it all one way, or the other.

Back to my daughter.  Despite being preschool aged, and relatively new to gaming, even she has legitimately beat us a few times.  The fact that it supports such a wide skill range, yet can still be fun for everyone, is such a big win.  Over the last several months, UCH is the game that she has asked to play with me the most.

The only con I can think of is that this game is capped at a max of four players.  I bet it would play just fine at five, or maybe even six players.  There have been a few times when we've had that many people that wanted to be included.  It was a slight bummer, as it felt like a lost opportunity.

[h1]Items and Modifiers[/h1]

Many items will feel familiar to anyone playing platformers, but there's another feature that provides extra depth: items you place can [i]interact[/i] with each other.  For example, you can stick a crossbow to a platform, which is stuck to a rotating wheel.  You now have a rotating, shooting platform!  That's a simple example, but the possibilities branch out from there.  You can create some interesting contraptions, or wacky chain reactions that spice up the competition.  After playing a few hours, you can get some wild ideas for creating your own custom levels.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3010480427

The modifiers change how the game is played, which can turn an experienced player back to a novice, leveling the playing field.  Things like gravity, projectile speed, friction, jetpack mode (to name a few) can be modified or activated, which force you to relearn the feel of the game.  My daughter started beating us when we used the modifier to flip the level upside down.  For some reason our old brains couldn't adjust quickly for that, but hers did!

[h1]Achievements[/h1]

I earned 100% of the achievements after 39 hours of play.  Overall, the achievements are pretty fitting, and reasonable.  None were misleading, nor tricky.  The seven rarest achievements aren't hard, they just take the most game time to earn (e.g. collecting outfits, scoring comeback points, and playing enough sudden death games).

[h1] Ultimate Chicken Horse: An Unforgettable Multiplayer Gem [/h1]

Ultimate Chicken Horse may seem like your typical 2D platformer at first glance, but it's so much more. This multiplayer game is addictive and a sheer delight.

In Ultimate Chicken Horse, up to four players dive into a 2D platforming stage simultaneously. You start each round by selecting a platform, object, or hazard to place on the stage. It's a brilliantly executed concept, making it one of the standout multiplayer games of 2017.

While the visuals may appear simple and goofy initially, they grow on you over time. The quirky charm of the characters singing and dancing is infectious. Despite being incredibly fun, Ultimate Chicken Horse has a few downsides. The interface is inconsistent, making navigation a bit tricky. Additionally, the game offers only two main play modes, which, while enjoyable, could benefit from more variety.

In conclusion, if you love 2D platformers and multiplayer gaming, Ultimate Chicken Horse is a must-have. Its seamless blend of platforming and creativity guarantees hours of unforgettable fun.

The Glorious Chaos: Why Ultimate Chicken Horse Reigns Supreme in the Party Game Arena
While the realm of party games boasts a plethora of contenders, few titles manage to capture the essence of competitive camaraderie quite like Ultimate Chicken Horse. This deceptively simple platformer with a delightfully devious twist transcends the boundaries of the genre, transforming friendly competition into a hilarious spectacle of gleeful sabotage and triumphant (or sometimes tragic) platforming.  But what exactly elevates Ultimate Chicken Horse from a good party game to the champion of the genre? Let's delve into the intricate mechanics, the unbridled creativity, and the infectious laughter that solidify this game's place at the pinnacle of party game glory.

A Recipe for Laughter: Ingredients Perfectly Blended

At its core, Ultimate Chicken Horse offers a delightfully straightforward objective: reach the goal before your opponents.  However, the path to victory is fraught with peril, and that peril is self-inflicted.  Here's the ingenious twist: players take turns building a treacherous obstacle course, strategically placing a variety of platforms, traps, and hazards.  This level-building phase becomes a delightful exercise in controlled malice.  You can opt for the classic pitfalls and swinging hammers, or unleash your inner mad scientist with ice cannons that launch unsuspecting competitors skyward.  The key lies in striking a balance – create a course that's challenging but fair for you to navigate, but fiendishly difficult for your friends.

The beauty lies in the unexpected.  Just when you think you've mastered a course, your friend unveils a devious new trap, sending you plummeting to a hilarious demise.  The resulting laughter isn't malicious, but rather a shared joy in the orchestrated chaos.  Every round presents a new puzzle to solve, a new opportunity to outsmart your friends, and most importantly, a fresh wave of side-splitting moments.

A Canvas for Creativity: Unleashing Your Inner Architect of Mayhem

Ultimate Chicken Horse isn't just about winning; it's about expressing your own unique brand of sadistic creativity.  The level creation tools offer a surprising depth, allowing you to craft courses that range from the deceptively simple to the mind-bogglingly complex.  Want to create a haunted mansion riddled with hidden spike traps? Go for it.  Feel like replicating a classic game show obstacle course? The tools are at your disposal.  This freedom allows players to tailor the experience to their group's preferences, ensuring endless entertainment.

Furthermore, the sheer variety of unlockable items adds another layer of strategic depth.  New traps, movement options, and purely cosmetic doodads provide players with the tools to personalize their playstyle and leave their signature mark on every course.  This constant influx of new content keeps the game fresh and encourages players to experiment and refine their devious course-building strategies.

Beyond the Competition: A Celebration of Friendship (Through Laughter)

While competition is undoubtedly a core aspect of Ultimate Chicken Horse, the true magic lies in the camaraderie it fosters.  The shared experience of triumph and (more likely) hilarious defeat creates an undeniable bond between players.  The game thrives on a healthy dose of friendly ribbing – you might curse your friend's fiendish contraption one round, only to unleash an even more diabolical trap the next.  This back-and-forth banter fuels the laughter and keeps the atmosphere light and playful.

The Verdict: A Crown Well Deserved

Ultimate Chicken Horse isn't simply a party game; it's an experience.  It's a crucible for laughter, a breeding ground for creative problem-solving, and a testament to the power of shared experiences.  While other party games might offer fleeting amusement, Ultimate Chicken Horse cultivates a unique brand of chaotic joy that keeps players coming back for more.  So, the next time you're looking for a game that guarantees laughter, side-splitting defeats, and a celebration of playful competition, look no further than Ultimate Chicken Horse.  It might just be the reigning champion of party game mayhem.

[h1] Ultimate Chicken Horse is a really fun multiplayer game with some bugs and online issues. [/h1]

Ultimate Chicken Horse (UCH) is a Level Designer-like Platformer. When you're in a level with other people, you can add platforms and traps each round. When everyone's done placing their objects, you then play the level. Your job is to be the only person to get to the goal, and prevent the other players to also succeed. If everyone makes it to the end, nobody gets points for that round (unless someone got an object called a Coin.). If everyone dies, nobody gets points for that round.

The controls when the level you're in takes some time to get use to. To me, they were really floaty the first time I played the game, which caused some accidental fails (like accidentally falling through a small gap). While they do need to get use to, the control layout is simple and easy to learn. I played this game with my Ps3 controller (I did some thing that makes my computer think my Ps3 controller is a Xbox 360 controller.), and the controls never got confusing, but since they're floaty in this game, again, they need to get use to.

When in the Build-like Mode, you can place 1 object every round (but I think you can change the amount of objects you can place down in the rules). In Party Mode, you and the other players get 4-5 random objects to choose from every round. If you see an object you want, you need to be quick, since the other players can take that object away from you. In Freeplay Mode, you get to select 1 object of your choice every round. If you want to place down a trap? You can do that if you want! Want to delete an object someone placed? You can do that if you want!

If you're the host, you can change the rules for your game. You can increase rounds, change the Game Mode, etc. So if you want your game to be different or more interesting, you can try to do that.

At the start of the game, you only get 3 levels, 4 characters, and no outfits. In order to get more levels/characters/outfits, you need to find these boxes with a "?" on them in the levels you have. If there is a box, a ? appears on a level in the Lobby. In order to get the boxes, you just need to touch them or put a trap next to them. It's easier than it sounds.

The Soundtrack and Artstyle are really good. Can't say anything else.

There are problems with the game: Bugs and Online Issues.

-When I was playing with other people I don't know, one of them said that they couldn't select an object, even though he was pressing the left mouse button on the object he wanted. Because of this issue, he/she couldn't put any objects down, only the the two players and I.
-I put stairs on a rotating object that had honey on it. At first, the stairs rotated like I wanted to, but then the stairs stopped rotating and was at a different place the next round.

I've encountered more bugs, but those are the bugs I can think of right now.

-When playing Online, things are out of sync at times. Like for example: I jump into a saw that's rotating, and I fail. The next player jumps, and even though it looks like he/she touched the saw, he/she is still going. Or like an arrow hits a player, and he/she's still going.
-Some things do disappear from a player's view. Sometimes an object disappears on a player's screen, which might screw them over.

Overall, if you want a really fun party game, Ultimate Chicken Horse is for you! Don't want to get 4 copies of the game? No worries! You can hook up 4 controllers to your computer and play the game together, just like that. In my opinion, 15 dollars is worth it for the super fun gameplay that never gets old.

Highly Recommended!

I know my time here seems not like much, but trust me when I say I have over two years of experience in this game. It is so worth the money, if you're looking for a fun party game to play with friends online or your family. There's even a feature to share the controller with others, making multiple controller multiplayer optional. Unlocking characters, outfits, levels and the like is very fun in the way that you collect them. Playing this game with anyone is sure to guarantee a few laughs.

Now, the game is a party game as I've mentioned, but the way you play it is very interesting. You gain objects from a "Party Box" at the start of each round of play, granting you an option between a few objects differing from traps to blocks to glue. As you continue placing blocks throughout the game, the goal is to make something challenging enough so that the other players can't beat it, but not too hard that you can't beat it. And with four people maximum placing these objects every round, things are bound to become chaotic. Machines of rotating wrecking balls, slippery ice platforms, hockey stick shooters shooting the puck into cannon launchers...
It's a very fun game to play with other people, as I've mentioned. They also do regular updates for the game, with the major ones adding a new character, alternate character costume for the new character, and a map with new music. Some of the maps are very fun with their gimmicks, like the Space map where the higher up you get, the lower your gravity becomes as you get closer to the UFO, or the Ballroom map, where the starting location changes each round. The game also has modifiers for your games, like double jumping or transformations after death. But this game has a form of user generated content... custom levels.
Custom levels are amazing. It allows anyone to create a level, whether that be a tight precision level like Ebb and Flow, or Super Mario Brothers world 1-1. Creators of custom levels get a lot of freedom with their levels, being able to select the music, background, and goal placement. They can even upload levels that are part of an existing vanilla UCH level, with addons. If you create something amazing during one of you and your friend's UCH rounds, you can save it in the current state, and upload it to the LevelNET.

Overall, this game is certainly worth the money. Very fun party game, even if you don't have friends to play it with. Playing solo online is still a blast! 10/10 game. BTW sheep's my favorite character :)

This title is one that I was interested in from the moment I came across it prior to its actual release. As an avid fan of platformers and games where you have a certain degree of creative control (level editors), this game fit me like a glove. And once I saw that the game was going to recieve the online treatment, I knew I needed it [b][i]ASAP[/i][/b].

I have no regrets.

On its surface, the gameplay is your average platformer. You can move with WASD, jump with the spacebar, and interact with certain elements of the world with your mouse. There is a wall jump mechanic, and you can even single wall jump. The best part: it all feels very fluid and responsive. But once you add in the multiplayer race aspect and the level customization, the game becomes much, [i]much[/i] more complicated. You want to make it possible, but you also want to make it very difficult so that you and only you can finish. You also want to figure out the fastest way to complete the level (which is set up differently every time you play) so that you have higher chances of winning.

There is a very good variety of level gimmicks available to you, but most of them need to be unlocked. That's not necessarily a bad thing though: the two stages that are available to you from the get-go, while fairly basic, are good for honing your skills in the game in a relatively safe environment. My personal favorite stage is unfortunately the one that you unlock last, but I can't really fault the developers for putting it there because the gimmick is fairly eye-straining.

For all you fans of hats out there (and I know you are out there), the game offers a decent selection of characters and character specific cosmetic items for use in game. All characters are balanced equally, so no one will get an advantage if they choose to use one character over another. The current build of the online beta as of the time of me writing this review has some issues with cosmetics, so I would recommend local play if you can swing it if you want to use them.

Finally, the current online beta runs exceptionally well for being a beta. There are public games available for anyone at most times of the day, and hosting a public game is as simple as specifying a region and pressing a button. If you don't have people to play with locally, you can probably find someone online to play with. Be warned: there is no chat right now, but one might be planned for the future. If you feel the need for a chat, I would recommend waiting for a bit before purchasing. Last I checked there is an emote system coming soon, but even then I'm aware that doesn't work for everyone.

You will progressively unlock not only new levels, but also new characters and their outfits, which are super cute and are one of the shining points of this party game.

The game also has tons of replayability, since it allows you to customise most of the rules to suit your play style. And it has a Steam Workshop where players share the levels they design, so you would never run out of something new to play.

The only downside is that online players are not all very friendly. However, if you intend to play mainly with your friends and family, hesitate no more!
